question: In the Robson Ten-Group Classification System (TGCS), which group represents women with a previous caesarean section, singleton cephalic presentation, and gestation of 37 weeks or more — and why is this group the most important to monitor in Indian hospitals?

answers.text: Group 1 — nulliparous, single, cephalic, term, in spontaneous labour; it is important because it has the largest absolute number of deliveries

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Group 1 covers nulliparous women in spontaneous labour, not those with a previous CS. While Group 1 has high absolute numbers, it is not the biggest driver of rising CS rates in India.

answers.text: Group 5 — previous caesarean section, singleton cephalic, 37 weeks or more; it is the single largest contributor to the overall CS rate in most Indian hospitals because it captures the cycle of repeat CS

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Group 5 (previous CS, term, singleton cephalic) is the Robson 'linchpin'. Once a woman has had one CS, subsequent deliveries are almost always by CS — creating a self-perpetuating cycle. In most Indian hospitals, Group 5 contributes the largest proportion to the overall CS rate.

answers.text: Group 6 — all nulliparous women with a single breech presentation; it drives CS rates because breech is always an indication for CS

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Group 6 is nulliparous single breech at term; while breech is often delivered by CS, the absolute numbers are smaller. Previous uterine scar (Group 5) is the dominant driver in Indian facilities.

answers.text: Group 10 — all women with a singleton in a transverse or oblique lie or with a major placenta praevia; it is important because these are emergencies

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Group 10 covers transverse/oblique lies and major placenta praevia. These are high-acuity cases but a small proportion of deliveries and not the primary driver of overall CS rates.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Robson groups. Group 5 — previous CS, term, singleton cephalic — is the key group because it captures the cycle of repeat CS that drives overall rates in Indian hospitals.
Excellent. Group 5 (previous CS, term singleton, cephalic) is the cornerstone of CS audit in India. Monitoring VBAC rates in this group is the most effective lever for reducing the overall CS rate.
